claims.text: Increasing interface thickness in CoCrFeMnNi-based HEA multilayers shifts the dominant creep mechanism from dislocation-mediated creep to diffusion-mediated creep.
The initial CoCrFeMnNi-based multilayers have highly coherent, thin interfaces approximately 2 nm thick.
Changing deposition parameters can increase interface thickness from approximately 2 nm to 20 nm.
Increasing interface thickness reduces interface coherency.
Creep behavior should be tested at 700–900 °C under constant stress or load in an inert environment.
Interface thickness and coherency are the structural variables mediating the creep response of the stacked HEA layers.
Thin, highly coherent interfaces obstruct dislocations.
Creep at thin, highly coherent interfaces remains predominantly dislocation-mediated.
Thicker, less coherent interfaces enhance pathways for atomic diffusion.
Enhanced interfacial diffusion causes a transition to diffusion-mediated creep.
Thin, coherent multilayers will exhibit lower creep rates than multilayers with thick, less coherent interfaces.
Thick, less coherent interfaces will produce higher creep rates dominated by diffusion.
Monolithic or coarse-grained CoCrFeMnNi specimens with little interface area deform primarily through dislocation-mediated creep over relevant temperatures and stresses.
At interface thicknesses greater than 50 nm, additional microstructural changes could obscure the proposed creep-mechanism transition.
Above 900 °C, additional microstructural changes could obscure the proposed creep-mechanism transition.
The critical interface thickness for the proposed transition is not established and may vary with composition or processing.
TEM observations of dislocation structures and compositional analysis of interfaces can distinguish the proposed mechanisms.
